previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, and G-tube dependence was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and inability to maintain oral intake, leading to dehydration and acute kidney injury. She was hydrated with IV fluids, which resolved her renal dysfunction. Persistent nausea and decreased G-tube output prompted imaging, which revealed malposition of the tube tip in the duodenum. The tube was successfully replaced with a shorter one positioned in the stomach antrum, improving venting. During admission, she reported suicidal ideation, which was evaluated by psychiatry; it was determined to be partially attention-seeking, and a sitter was discontinued after she expressed future-oriented goals. Nutrition support was limited by lack of insurance coverage for TPN and ethanol lock line care. She was discharged home with improved pain, stable mental status, and instructions to eat small meals, maintain hydration, and follow up with her outpatient team.
problems: Dyspepsia and other specified disorders of function of stomach

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with sclerosing mesenteritis and chronic abdominal pain with 
G tube to decompression, presented to the ED with failure to 
thrive. She was discharged 3 days prior to admission and was 
readmitted with worsening vomiting and poor PO intake.

Active issues:
# Nausea and vomiting: Patient with extensive history of 
abdominal surgeries and past TPN use, which was discontinued in 
___ for insurance reasons. She has had frequent admissions 
due to nausea and dehydration. She was discharged a few days 
prior to presentation and reported increased output from her G 
tube at home along with nausea and vomiting with poor PO intake. 
On presentation, she had Cr of 1.4 from baseline 0.9-1.1 ___s metabolic alkalosis and hypokalemia. Electrolytes were 
repleted and she was given IV fluids, with complete resolution 
of metabolic abnormalities. KUB showed evidence of ileus but was 
unchanged from prior studies. Patient continued to report nausea 
throughout admission, but was hemodynamically and metabolically 
stable and did not require further IV fluids after ___ she was 
only observed to vomit on one occasion. She was medically 
cleared for discharge on ___, however, the patient was 
reluctant to go home because ""I'll just be back in three days."" 
She appealed her discharge to Medicare. It was upheld and she 
was discharged to home on ___.

# Aspiration pneumonitis: Patient reported aspiration while 
vomiting ___ with transient tachycardia and low grade fever. 
She developed crackles in left lower lobe with left lower lobe 
retrocardiac opacity on X-ray. Thought to be pneumonitis rather 
than pneumonia as white count was not elevated and patient was 
afebrile and hemodynamically stable for the rest of her stay, 
however levofloxacin was started given persistent cough and 
e.coli grew in sputum.
.
# Suicidality:  Because of ongoing suicidality, she was 
initially placed on 1:1 sitter on admission, and psychiatry was 
consulted.  She was continued on her home psychiatric 
medications. Sitter was discontinued following evaluation by 
psychiatry, as patient denied active suicidal ideation at that 
time and there was concern about sitter contributing to 
regression and dependence on hospital for emotional needs. On 
___, patient found trying to cut her wrist with a pin. Patient 
distraught, complaining of increased pain and that she was 
feeling alone and uncared for. She stated that she was trying to 
cut her wrists and ""it didn't work"". She was unable to contract 
for safety, and in fact said that if her calls to nursing were 
not answered quickly enough, she would likely try to injure 
herself. Sitter was re-ordered and then the next morning, denied 
suicidal ideation, the sitter was discontinued. She was able to 
contract for safety and was not suicidal on discharge. 
. 
# IV Access: As a result of long-term tunneled line use, this 
patient has poor central intravenous access, limited to femoral 
lines (e.g. no IJ or Subclavian access), so policy with her is 
to refrain from placing central venous access outside of the ___ 
suite except in urgent or emergent situations.  Line needs were 
discussed with ___ and midline was placed, removed 
prior to discharge.
.
